payload.note: Designing the guard predicate shape; decision to follow before any code.

payload.because: the violation must name the decision, so the predicate belongs on the same event as the clause it enforces — a side file drifts from the rule it claims to guard. Same one-field-one-concept grain as D1, and `guard` REQUIRES `rule`: a guard with no clause has nothing to cite when it fires. Globs over regex — agent-authored patterns must be safe to compile and cheap inside the 100ms hook budget, and every ambiguity resolves to a non-match. `path:` anchors at a segment boundary so it matches the tail of the ABSOLUTE paths hooks log (portable across machines, which absolute matching is not); `cmd:` matches as a substring, because `cmd:npm publish` silently never firing would be a guard that reads as compliance. Non-retroactive — a guard only sees events after its own decision, or the first thing it flags is the work that motivated it. Warn, never block: Stop's one deliberate exit 2 stays write-back only (BD2/BD22), a false-positive block stops real work, and inferring intent to avoid false positives would need a model call (SPEC zero-model-API-calls).
payload.chose: `guard` as an optional companion field to `rule` on decision_logged — `path:`/`cmd:` domain-prefixed comma-separated globs (leading `!` exempts) evaluated by the fold against file_touched/command_run events logged AFTER that decision; violations are derived state surfaced as warnings only (doctor axis, UserPromptSubmit line, and the existing Stop block message)
payload.over: a hand-written .sofar/guards.json; regex predicates; blocking Stop on violation; deriving the predicate from the rule prose
payload.rule: A guard warns, never blocks: a guard violation must never change any exit code, and Stop's exit 2 stays write-back-only.

git add -A && git commit -q -F - <<'EOF' && git log --oneline -1
5.1-5.3: decision guards — the mechanical tier (D3)

A rule states a standing constraint in prose; a guard is the half of that
same clause a machine can check. It rides the SAME decision_logged event —
the warning has to name the decision, and a side file drifts from the rule
it claims to guard — and it only ever warns.

- schema: `guard` on decision_logged, valid only alongside `rule`; the
  grammar (packages/schema/src/guards.ts) is `path:`/`cmd:` glob lists with
  `!` exemptions. path anchors at a segment boundary so it matches the tail
  of the absolute paths hooks log; cmd matches as a substring. Not regex —
  agent-authored [redacted] must be safe to compile inside the shim budget.
- fold: violations derived during replay, so a guard only ever sees the work
  that followed it; deduped per (rule, session, subject), capped at 100.
